title: Beating the SDP bound for the floor layout problem: A simple combinatorial idea
contribution: A combinatorial dual-bounding scheme that aggregates exact optima of small restricted subproblems; for (1D-)floor layout it provably matches or beats lifted LP/SDP and ad-hoc SDP bounds and computationally beats Gurobi's dual bound at equal time.
problem_entry: SDP hierarchies give strong MIP dual bounds but are too large to build in memory, and floor layout has mature heuristics but immature bound technology (pp. 1-2, 4).
key_idea: Solve the problem exactly on variable subsets, turn each optimum into a valid inequality on that subset's objective part, aggregate in a master relaxation; nested subset families give a polynomial hierarchy (Thm 2.2, Prop 2.3, pp. 3-4; Prop 3.1, p. 6).
assumptions: Any set Q with finite optimum and outer approximations of projections (p. 3); FLP unary formulation (2) and 1D-FLP formulation (3) (pp. 4-6).
proof_devices: Midpoint of two mirror-image feasible layouts, with variables outside cut supports zeroed, shows disjoint-support valid inequalities cannot beat omega_k (Prop 4.1, pp. 8-9)
Explicit zero-value LP point shows LP relaxation is trivial; bound inequalities lift it to omega_2 (pp. 7-8)
Equivalence: lifted LP, lifted SDP and Takouda SDP all equal closed-form omega_2 (Props 4.2-4.3, pp. 9-10; proofs in appendices not read)
experiments: Julia/JuMP, Gurobi 6.0.4, Mosek 7.1 on a laptop; same-bound time comparison vs lifted LP/SDP (CB < 1e-4 s, SDP times out at 15+ components) and equal-time gap comparison vs Gurobi, CB better on most instances (pp. 11-13).
positioning: Against SDP hierarchies (Lasserre, Lovasz-Schrijver, Sherali-Adams) and the Takouda et al. 2005 FLP SDP; uses own sparse-cut papers to motivate Prop 4.1 (pp. 1, 8, 9-10).
writing: Assessment sentences stated plainly ('Our assessment is...', p. 12); computational claim restricted explicitly to formulation (3) (p. 12); 'cautiously optimistic' about true gaps (p. 14).
limits_future: No comparison with Amaral 2009/Anjos et al. 1D-FLP bounds, serial implementation, gaps against solver incumbent (pp. 11-12, 14); no future-work section.

negative result for sparse disjoint-support cuts; computational claim restricted to formulation (3)
no exact ceiling; gaps measured against Gurobi's best feasible solution

title: The strength of multi-row aggregation cuts for sign-pattern integer programs
contribution: For sign-pattern IPs (no cancellation under aggregation) the aggregation closure is 2-approximated by the original 1-row closure (tight), but the 2-aggregation closure can be arbitrarily stronger than both the aggregation closure and the original 2-row closure.
problem_entry: Solvers use aggregation cuts; Bodur et al. showed packing/covering aggregation adds little; the conjectured reason (no cancellation) is tested on sign-pattern IPs where cancellation is impossible (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Compare closures by multiplicative alpha-approximation across 1-row, aggregation, 2-aggregation and original 2-row closures (Defs 2-4, Thms 1-3, pp. 3-4; Table 1, p. 5).
assumptions: (J+,J-) sign-pattern polyhedra, non-negative data, A_ij <= b_i on J+, rational data (Def 1, p. 3).
proof_devices: One-row sign-pattern polyhedron P subset 2P^I, then intersect over aggregations using scaling commuting with intersection (Prop 3, Obs 1, p. 6)
Parametric counterexample families with LP/IP ratio M/2 and M/4+1 while A2 = P^I (pp. 6-7)
positioning: Generalises Bodur-Del Pia-Dey-Molinaro-Pokutta packing result; relates to Marchand-Wolsey aggregation heuristics and multi-row cut literature (pp. 1-2).
writing: Short ORL note: results stated in section 2.2 with a summary table including an open '?' cell, proofs in section 3; no conclusion (pp. 4-5, 9).
limits_future: Case 2-A vs A2 with m = 3 open (Table 1, p. 5); second part of Theorem 3 not written out (p. 9).

title: New SOCP relaxation and branching rule for bipartite bilinear programs
contribution: Shows the convex hull of a one-row bipartite bilinear set is SOCP representable, that the intersection of these hulls is at least as strong as SDP intersected with the Boolean quadric polytope, and that a volume-based branching rule plus a polyhedral outer approximation beats BARON on dual bounds for finite element model updating.
problem_entry: Bipartite bilinear programs and a new structural-engineering application (FE model updating), entered by copying the single-constraint relaxation idea of integer programming (pp. 2, 4, 15).
key_idea: Extreme points of a one-row BBP set have at most one edge's variables fractional, so the hull is a convex hull of finitely many SOCP pieces; branching point chosen to minimise total hull volume of two-variable pieces (Thm 1, pp. 2-3; section 2.2, p. 4; section 4.2, pp. 12-14).
assumptions: Box [0,1], equality rows; computationally a light per-row version with tangential polyhedral outer approximation, without guarantees (pp. 2, 4-5, 17-18).
proof_devices: Extreme-point argument: two fractional x-variables lie in the relative interior of a linear equation after fixing the rest (Prop 1, p. 7)
Convex hull of a finite union of SOCP-representable sets over a partition of extreme points (Lemma 3, p. 6)
Split equality into <= and >= hulls (Lemma 1, p. 5)
Containment in SDP and QBP relaxations via projection notation (Thm 2, Props 6-7, pp. 9-11; skimmed)
experiments: 10 FE-model-updating instances, 10 h limit; polyhedral SOCP best root bound among Mc/SDP/SDP+Mc but below McCormick discretisation; Python B&B with new rule gaps 1.5-27.9% vs BARON 40.8-90.7%; ablation with McCormick + new rule 52.6-99.2% (pp. 17-21).
positioning: Generalises one-row hull results and contrasts set convexification with function envelopes; other SOCP relaxations for QCQP are weaker than SDP (pp. 3-4).
writing: Results overview in section 2 before proofs, honest 'Unfortunately' caveat on the light relaxation (p. 5), Remark 2 states what cannot be proved (p. 4).
limits_future: Exponential extended formulation, no guarantee for the light version, McCormick discretisation stronger at root (pp. 4-5, 19); no conclusion section.

title: Lower bounds on the lattice-free rank for packing and covering integer programs
contribution: Lower bounds on split, multi-branch split and lattice-free rank of packing sets (and split rank of covering polyhedra) as the log of the integrality gap divided by the log of a per-round approximation factor, with tight factors for split cuts.
problem_entry: Rank is the standard strength measure of cut families, but few results tie it to the integrality gap (p. 1).
key_idea: Packing invariance plus constant approximation give rank >= log2(zLP/zI)/log2(alpha_M) (Prop 1, p. 4); tools to verify both (Thms 1-2, pp. 4-5).
assumptions: Packing/covering with non-negative rational data and well-behavedness (p. 2).
proof_devices: Telescoping product of per-round approximation ratios (Prop 1, p. 7)
Reduce packing invariance to closure of the lattice-free family under coordinate restriction (Thm 1, pp. 4-5)
Transfer constant approximation from polyhedra to general packing sets via arbitrarily close inner polyhedra (Thm 2, p. 5)
positioning: First link of split rank to integrality gap; generalises a CG-rank result; split results not implied by aggregation-closure results of Bodur et al. (pp. 5-7).
writing: Main results section with proof overviews before proofs; explicit statement of what is unknown (pp. 4-7).
limits_future: Covering result not extended to k-lattice-free rank because well-behavedness of that closure is unknown (p. 7); no conclusion section.

title: Optimization-driven scenario grouping
contribution: A scenario-grouping preprocessing step for scenario decomposition that maximises a proxy (computed from evaluated candidate solutions) of the non-anticipativity bound improvement, with complexity results, a finitely convergent algorithm, and computations that close all previously unsolved SIPLIB SSCH instances.
problem_entry: Choosing groups by true bound improvement would require solving the grouped stochastic programs; prior groupings are random, k-means or enumerative (pp. 4-5).
key_idea: Proxy theta_m from candidate solutions upper-bounds group bound improvement and is exact when the group optimum is a candidate; maximise sum theta_m under group size P (Prop 1, eqs. (7)-(8), p. 8); iterate in Algorithm 2 (p. 13).
assumptions: Two-stage stochastic programs with finitely many scenarios; experiments on 0-1 first stage; finite feasible region for Algorithm 2 (pp. 13, 15).
proof_devices: P = 2 as maximum-weight matching (Prop 2, pp. 8-9)
NP-hardness at P = 3 by reduction from Partition into Triangles (Prop 3, p. 9)
Finite convergence by enumeration of the finite feasible set (Prop 4, p. 13)
experiments: SIPLIB on LLNL cluster, CPLEX 12.5, 5 seeds, 3 h: OSG P=4 solves all SSCH instances incl. four previously unsolved; PySP progressive hedging on stochastic unit commitment: OSG gaps an order of magnitude smaller than random/k-means but longer preprocessing (pp. 15-18, 26-29).
positioning: Contrasts with solution-driven clustering (Crainic et al., Song-Luedtke) and enumerative bound hierarchies (EGSO); calls Dey et al. 2018 bounds data-independent (p. 5).
writing: Three-item contribution list (p. 4); conclusion recommends grouping 'anytime' scenario decomposition is used (p. 34).
limits_future: Preprocessing cost, random choice of which solutions to evaluate, extensive form preferable when solvable (p. 28); future: risk-averse and chance-constrained programs (p. 34).

title: Exact augmented Lagrangian duality for mixed integer quadratic programming
contribution: For convex MIQP the augmented Lagrangian dual closes the gap asymptotically for level-bounded penalties and exactly with a finite, polynomially sized weight for any norm penalty, generalising the MILP result of Feizollahi-Ahmed-Sun.
problem_entry: Lagrangian dual of MIQP has a gap; exact ALD known for MILP; penalty-weight size rarely discussed (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Use the MIQP-in-NP decomposition of mixed-integer polyhedra into polytope + integer cone pieces and small-complexity bounding boxes to bound x uniformly and get a polynomial rho* (Thms 10-11, p. 3; Lemmas 14-15, pp. 5-6; Thm 22, p. 12).
assumptions: Rational PSD Q, rational data, MIQP feasible and bounded (Assumption 1, p. 2); penalty proper, lsc, level-bounded (Assumption 17, p. 6) or a norm.
proof_devices: Flowcharts linking lemmas to each main theorem (pp. 3-4)
Uniform positive gap delta of the penalty on infeasible points gives finite rho* (Thm 21, p. 11)
L-infinity rewrite with scalar w and rho-independent bound on x (Thm 22, Lemma 23, p. 12)
Decomposition and small-complexity lemmas from MIQP-in-NP [7] (Lemmas 14-15, pp. 5-6)
positioning: Generalises Feizollahi-Ahmed-Sun MILP exact ALD [9]; builds on Del Pia-Dey-Molinaro [7] (pp. 1-2, 5).
writing: Numbered three-point contribution list (p. 2), flowcharts of proof dependencies (pp. 3-4), conclusion with honest caveats (p. 17).
limits_future: Penalised subproblem may be harder and still nonconvex; future separable exact algorithms (ADMM-like) (p. 17).

title: Subset selection in sparse matrices
contribution: Subset Selection is solvable in polynomial time when the data matrix is block diagonal with constant-width blocks plus a constant number of dense columns, via hyperplane arrangements in the coupling-parameter space and a proximity lemma for optimal supports.
problem_entry: Large MIO models need data parameters that give polynomial algorithms; sparsity pattern (1) is open for integer LP without bounded entries; Subset Selection asked for this pattern (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Reduce to 2^k problems with coupling variables as parameters; for fixed parameters the optimal support comes from pairwise linear comparisons, so an O(n^k)-cell hyperplane arrangement yields polynomially many candidate supports, each solved by least squares (Lemma 1, pp. 6-7; Lemma 2, Claim 1, p. 8; p. 6).
assumptions: M of form (1) with constant block widths and constant k; 2-norm (extends to p-norms) (p. 3).
proof_devices: Hyperplane arrangement theorem bounds the number of parameter regions with fixed optimal support (p. 6; Claim 1, p. 8)
Proximity of optimal block supports between sigma and sigma+1 (Lemma 3, p. 11)
Explicit small matrices separating the class from eigenvalue, covariance-sparsity and restricted-isometry tractable classes (pp. 3-5)
positioning: Contrasts with Gao-Li eigenvalue condition, Das-Kempe sparse covariance, compressive-sensing RIP results; connects to N-fold and tree-width integer programming (pp. 2-5).
writing: Main theorem on p. 3 with explicit running time, overview of the algorithm before proofs, diagonal case first (pp. 3, 5-7).
limits_future: Large exponents; NP-hard if any block width or k is free (p. 3); no conclusion section or implementation.
